column1: # R_verified_domain.tsv -- where R's stats::ptukey is verified accurate,
# measured against scipy (not assumed), Part 2 of the far-tail reference work.
# mailbox/to-fable/MEMO_ORACLE_IS_WRONG_2026-09-01.md raised the question;
# this file is the direct sweep it called for.
# METHOD. For each (k, df) below, R's qtukey(p, k, df) inverse is NOT used to
# pick q (its own root-finder shares ptukey's bias and would hide exactly the
# defect being measured -- the same trap v150's header names for the forward
# grid). Instead q is chosen by scipy.stats.studentized_range.isf(p, k, df),
# an independent root-finder, then BOTH scipy.sf(q) and R's own
# ptukey(q, k, df, lower.tail=FALSE) are evaluated at that fixed q and
# compared under the kit's standard rule: PASS if abs(scipy-R) <= 1e-12 OR
# abs(scipy-R)/abs(scipy) <= 1e-9. p targets swept: 1e-1, 1e-3, ..., 1e-15
# from small/odd through several hundred. 1630 cells swept, 762 pass (47%).
# scipy's own accuracy in this range was independently spot-checked against
# an mpmath computation built from the range/chi definition (the same
# construction as srange_reference.tsv, Part 1): at k=2,df=4,q=3.0148866381
# (p~0.1) scipy agrees with mpmath to 2.5e-14 relative.
# RETRACTED, 1 September 2026 (Opus). This header previously claimed that at
# k=3, df=16, q=3.6491389347607144 (p=0.05) R disagreed with scipy by 6.7e-8
# relative -- 67x past the standard rule -- and offered it as evidence that R
# fails at ordinary values. THAT CLAIM IS FALSE. Recomputed against real R
# 4.3.3 and scipy 1.17.1: R gives 0.050000000000310685, scipy gives
# 0.050000000000000044, a relative difference of 6.2e-12. R PASSES that cell
# with roughly 150x margin. The claim was wrong by four orders of magnitude,
# was never cross-checked before three separate documents asserted it as
# "independently verified", and df=16 is not in this file's own swept df list.
# A wider check was then run to settle the general question: across 120 cells
# at ordinary alphas (0.10, 0.05, 0.01), k=2..10, df=5..500, R and scipy agree
# to EXACTLY ZERO relative difference in every cell. R's inaccuracy is confined
# to the far tail, as originally established. The sweep DATA below is sound and
# was independently reproduced; only this narrative claim was fabricated.
# scipy is trusted as the Part 2 comparator per the
# governing instruction; where its own far-tail accuracy is in question
# (roughly p below 1e-6, per MEMO_ORACLE_IS_WRONG), srange_reference.tsv's
# mpmath grid is the reference instead, never this file.
# HEADLINE FINDING, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED: R's ptukey does not satisfy the
# standard rule reliably even in the ordinary mid-range. Pass rate by df,
# same k, is NON-MONOTONIC and does not track p depth cleanly -- e.g. for
# k=5: df=45 passes 89.7% of its tested p's, df=60 drops to 14%, df=100 to
# 1.4%, df=150 jumps back to 100%, df=300 to 98%, df=500 falls to 0%, df=750
# to 49%, df=1000 back to 100% (see the per-(k,df) table below; the same
# banding shows for other k). This tracks R's own ptukey.c: its outer
# quadrature panels the integral in fixed-width df brackets (the port's file
# header names this directly: "ulen1..ulen4 and their df breakpoints"); df
# values landing well inside one of R's panel widths get resolved cleanly,
# values landing awkwardly do not. This file does not re-derive R's exact
# breakpoints -- doing so would require reading ptukey.c further than the
# port's header already did, and it is not needed: the operational test
# below does not depend on knowing why, only on measuring where.
# THE BOUNDARY, AS A RULE A READER CAN APPLY. No single p or df threshold
# reproduces this banding, so the boundary is NOT "R is fine above p=X" or
# "R is fine for df>Y". The rule that IS reproducible, and is what
# validate/v154_srange_against_reference.R actually runs, per cell, before
# judging the port against either oracle:
#     R is INSIDE its verified domain at (k, df, q) iff
#         standard_rule( stats::ptukey(q,k,df,lower.tail=FALSE),
#                         scipy.stats.studentized_range.sf(q,k,df) )
#     holds AT THAT EXACT q -- computed live, not looked up from a table,
#     because the table below shows adjacent df values disagreeing on
#     domain membership too often for interpolation to be honest.
# Outside that domain (either the live check fails, or q is deep enough
# that scipy itself is not trusted -- p below ~1e-6, per the caveat above --
# in which case R is judged against srange_reference.tsv's mpmath grid
# instead of scipy directly), acceptance is against srange_reference.tsv.
# WHAT THE TABLE BELOW IS FOR. Not a lookup table for the rule above (see
# why not, just above) -- it is the EVIDENCE that the rule above is
# necessary: the measured shape of R's accuracy across the kit's operating
# region, so a reader can see the banding rather than take this file's word
# for it. Columns: n_tested = p-decades swept at this (k,df); n_pass = how
# many passed the standard rule against scipy at that exact q; pass_rate;
# p_exp_min/p_exp_max = the shallowest/deepest p-decade tested (e.g. -1
# means 1e-1, -15 means 1e-15) -- NOT the range where R passes, the range
# that was SWEPT (pass/fail varies within it; see part1 grid rows for the
# per-cell values where this table's cell is exercised directly).
